events.subject_response: Police1/The Record reported that Rensselaer County spokesman Richard Crist said, ‘We look forward to answering this legal action.’ The report also says County Executive Steve McLaughlin, identified as Republican, maintained that he had no intention of dissolving the agreement; Bourgault and other sheriffs separately challenged the state law in federal court.
events.summary: New York’s attorney general and governor announced a state Supreme Court lawsuit alleging that the Rensselaer County Sheriff’s Office failed to terminate its ICE 287(g) agreement by the August 25 deadline under the Local Cops, Local Crimes Act. The state seeks an order compelling termination and declaring the agreement void; the allegations remain subject to court resolution.
events.reason_for_status: The official attorney general release documents a new civil enforcement filing and identifies the alleged statutory noncompliance. The current-window Police1 report independently confirms the filing and explicitly identifies Bourgault as Republican; prior reputable regional election reporting documents his Republican and Conservative affiliation. This is recorded as a court filing, not a final finding or criminal conviction; the official government record qualifies for automatic publication under the evidence rule.

The federal filing is separate from the New York Attorney General’s state enforcement lawsuit recorded above.
